Welcome—I'm so glad you're here with me. What if I told you that racism isn't just about individual choices or the occasional hateful act? It's actually a web of policies and ideas that quietly, and sometimes loudly, shape the world around us—often in ways we don't even notice.
Together, we're about to step into the world of How to Be an Antiracist by Ibram X. Kendi. Kendi doesn't let us off the hook with the idea of being neutral. Instead, he invites us to really look at our thoughts and actions, and asks: Are we supporting racism, or are we fighting against it? There's no sitting on the sidelines here.
This journey is personal—sometimes uncomfortably so. It means taking a deep, honest look at ourselves, and at the stories and systems that have shaped us. Through Kendi's own experiences, powerful research, and thoughtful reflection, we'll explore how the lines between racist and antiracist thinking show up in daily choices and the bigger structures we live in.
As we peel back these layers, you'll start to see how racism is woven into everyday life—from the rules that govern our communities to the beliefs we hold deep down. But here's the thing: Kendi also shows us how the fight for justice isn't just about standing against obvious prejudice. It's about actively building something better—fairer systems, kinder mindsets, and a future where equity isn't just a dream.
So, as we set out together, let’s get curious, stay open, and ask ourselves what it really means to move from awareness to real, meaningful action. Are you ready to explore what antiracism can look like, not just in the world, but in your own life? Let’s begin this important journey together.
